title: 艺术的反资本主义本体论：论艺术家作为反资本主义者的历史根源

zh: 艺术的反资本主义本体论：论艺术家作为反资本主义者的历史根源
en: Art’s anti-capitalist ontology: on the historical roots of the artist as an anti-capitalist

zh: 戴夫·比奇
en: DAVE BEECH

zh: 从历史上看，“艺术问题”——什么是艺术？——主要关涉对象的分类及其效果，尽管自1960年代以来，这一问题已有些转向对象经由制度程序被引导跨越艺术门槛的过程。
本文通过追溯艺术问题的历史，勾勒一条走出艺术对象本体论与艺术制度理论之间对立的道路；我认为，这一历史植根于围绕劳动的争论。我的观点并不是说，探究艺术定义的“真正”指涉物是艺术劳动或审美劳动（马尔库塞关于艺术作为非异化劳动的概念），
也不是说艺术家是决定某物是否为艺术的决定性因素（贾德的箴言）。
我的目标毋宁是，把艺术问题重新放回艺术、手艺、商业与工业之间对抗的历史及其遗产之中——这场对抗发生于欧洲从封建主义向资本主义过渡期间为使艺术凌驾于体力劳动之上而进行的长期斗争。
en: Historically, ‘the art question’ – what is art? – has been principally concerned with the classification of objects and their effects, although since the 1960s it has been redirected somewhat towards the institutional procedures by which objects are marshalled across the threshold of art.

This essay maps a route out of the opposition between an ontology of art objects and an institutional theory of art by retracing the history of the art question, which, I will argue, is rooted in disputes over labour. My point is not that the ‘real’ referent of inquiries into the definition of art is artistic or aesthetic labour (Marcuse’s concept of art as non-alienated labour),
nor that the artist is the decisive factor in determining what is or is not art (Judd’s dictum).

My aim, rather, is to resituate the art question within the history and legacies of the confrontation between art, handicraft, commerce and industry during the prolonged struggle in Europe to elevate art above manual labour during the transition from feudalism to capitalism.

zh: 耶拿浪漫派开创的对艺术本体论的探究，历史上源于从文艺复兴延续到18世纪中叶的争论：绘画、雕塑及相关艺术应如何归类、处于何种地位、具有哪些共同特征。

en: The inquiry into the ontology of art which was inaugurated by the Jena Romantics arose historically out of debates about the grouping, status and common features of painting, sculpture and related arts, which ran from the Renaissance to the middle of the eighteenth century.
Vasari’s category of the
and Batteux’s 1746 theory of the

bookend an ambitious project to draw a new line of demarcation within the hierarchy of the liberal and mechanical arts in which certain specified arts are grouped together and reclassified. The aim was to promote painting and sculpture (and related arts) from the mechanical to the liberal arts, but the struggle culminates instead with these arts being assigned a name of their own – the
, fine arts,
and cognate terms.

zh: 这一对绘画和雕塑（及相关艺术）进行历史性重新分类的插曲，不仅告诉我们艺术是什么，也告诉我们这个问题如何对我们具有意义，以及它如何可能以更令人满意的方式得到回答。我不打算去确认对象必须具有何种特征才能被归入艺术，也不打算把这一探究置换为对艺术那些受到严密巡查的边界之条件的考察，或承认能被纳入艺术范畴的东西没有界限；相反，我想通过重构艺术这一范畴如何经由偶然的社会过程而形成，来重新思考它的不确定性。
en: This episode in the historical reclassification of painting and sculpture (and related arts) has something to tell us not only about what art is but also about how this question comes to have a meaning for us, and how it might be answered in a more satisfactory way. In place of identifying the features that objects must have in order to be categorized as art, or displacing that inquiry to investigate the conditions of art’s heavily policed borders, or acknowledging that there is no limit to what can be included in the category of art, I want to reconsider the indeterminacy of art as a category by reconstructing how it was formed through contingent social processes.

zh: 尽管为绘画和雕塑（及相关艺术）提出的历史主张最终以所谓的对象属性——以及对这些对象的体验——得到表达，它们最初却被归属于各种劳动类型。艺术作品的显性品质最初被理解为特定劳动形式的结果；也就是说，是在每一门特定艺术内部生产一系列作品所需的心智能力与手工能力的具体结合。
我的论证重新强调劳动的重要性，但并不主张艺术是某种劳动的结果；我想把围绕艺术形成并不断重构的那个充满争议、不断移动的边界，描述为围绕劳动的各种斗争的高度编码化表征。我的意图是，把关于各类对象相对价值及其隐含本体论的问题，重新连接到一部关于与之相应的活动类型之差别的、挥之不去却大多未被承认的历史，从而澄清如下问题：艺术一方与手艺、制造业、商业和工业另一方之间是什么关系。
en: While the historical claims made for painting and sculpture (and related arts) ultimately came to be expressed in the alleged properties of objects – and the experience of them – they were initially assigned to types of labour. The ostensive qualities of works of art were initially understood as the result of specific forms of labour; that is to say, the concrete combination of mental and manual capacities needed to produce a range of products within each specific art.

My argument re-emphasizes the significance of labour, but instead of claiming that art is the result of a certain kind of labour I want to characterize the contested and shifting boundary that is formed and reformed around art as a highly codified representation of struggles over labour. My intention is to clarify questions about the relationship between art, on the one hand, and handicraft, manufacturing, commerce and industry, on the other, by reconnecting questions about the relative merits and implied ontologies of various categories of object to a lingering but largely unacknowledged history of the differentiation of types of activity appropriate to them.

zh: 从艺术话语中不时爆发的恐慌来看，艺术不是一种特定类型的对象，而是特定类型经济的效果。对某些艺术史家、批评家和艺术家来说，艺术的存在似乎永远受到威胁：一接触完全为商业利润而生产的文化，或者更严重地，一旦降入其中，艺术便遭威胁。充当这个反面角色的，可以是平面设计，也可以是文化产业、媚俗艺术或商品生产，以及任何数量的其他样本，但逻辑始终如一：艺术不是
也不是
，因此当艺术变得（更像）
或
时，它就遭到稀释或否定。T.J.克拉克在2000年的一次讲话中，带着某种紧迫感讲述了这则熟悉的故事：
en: To judge from the panic which erupts in the discourses of art every now and then, art is not a specific kind of object but the effect of a specific kind of economy. For certain art historians, critics and artists it seems the existence of art is perpetually threatened by its contact with, or – more seriously – its descent into, culture produced entirely for commercial gain. The stooge can be graphics or the culture industry or kitsch or commodity production, and any number of other specimens, but the logic remains: art is not
or
and therefore art is diluted or negated by becoming (more like)

. T.J. Clark, speaking in 2000, tells this familiar tale with some urgency:

或
的页面便会无情而单调地证实它——其真正含义难道不正是如此吗？它不仅不存在，艺术还以其不存在为荣。这种不存在正是艺术当前的重要主题之一……现代主义始终与它所赖以为生的表象领域保持着紧密而危险的邻近关系。
en: Is not visual art in the process of becoming simply and irrevocably  part of the apparatus of image life production? Is not this the real  sense of the much-noticed fact (a flip through the pages of
or

confirms the fact, relentlessly, monotonously) that the  one demarcation between visual art and the fashion industry, for  example, simply does not exist any longer? Not only does it not exist  but art glories in its non-existence. The non-existence is one of art’s  great present themes… Modernism always stood in close, dangerous  proximity to the realm of appearances it fed on.

zh: 克拉克理解在艺术与流行文化那些令人不适的接触点上开展工作的批判要求，但在此例中，在他看来，对艺术与商业文化之区分的政治化颠覆已经走得太远。

在这里，把艺术作为一种实践加以界分的意识形态划界，并非完全独立于其物质与经济条件。在我的分析中，我将尤其强调艺术作品特定生产方式的历史建构，包括那种赋予艺术家以特权位置的特殊社会分工。因此，按我的解读，克拉克对艺术邻近时尚产业的焦虑，是艺术与设计之间界线被彻底侵蚀的一个例子，也就是说，艺术变得只不过是一种商业活动；他之所以以时尚作为商业文化的例证，正是要突出这一点。他对艺术与商业之区分崩塌的分析，主要落在艺术作品本身，以及一代艺术家的意志涣散之上——他们不再忠实于审美劳动的现代主义罗曼司，不再坚持先锋派与媚俗艺术之间那种精英主义式的对立，也不再具备在否定实践中批判性地运用流行形式所必需的形式细察。
然而，这一分析所倚赖的，是对艺术与市场之间一种隐含对抗关系的敏锐感受。
en: Clark understands the critical demands of operating at the uncomfortable points of contact between art and popular culture, but in this instance the politically charged subversion of the distinction of art from commercial culture appears to him to have gone too far.

Here, the ideological demarcation of art as a practice is not completely independent from its material and economic conditions. In my analysis, emphasis will be placed in particular on the historical construction of a specific mode of production for artworks, including the specific social division of labour in which the artist is assigned a place of privilege. So, Clark’s anxieties about art’s proximity to the fashion industry, on my reading, is an instance of the complete erosion of the divide between art and design, that is to say of art becoming nothing but a commercial activity, which he highlights by taking fashion as the exemplification of commercial culture. His analysis of the collapse of the distinction between art and commerce falls mainly on artworks themselves and the failure of nerve of a generation of artists who no longer demonstrate fidelity to the modernist romance of aesthetic labour, or the elitist opposition of avant-garde and kitsch, or the formal scrutiny required for the critical deployment of popular forms within practices of negation.
What it rests on, though, is a keen sense of an implied antagonism between art and the marketplace.

zh: 我不想把这个具体例子说得过重。克拉克有他自己版本的这一叙事，即艺术受到商业化威胁，但这种思维模式很常见。安德烈亚·弗雷泽在2004年回顾她创作的一件作品时，把同一种对立用于某些不同的目的；那件作品的内容是与一位收藏家发生性关系：
en: I do not want to overstate the specific case. Clark has his own variant of this narrative of art’s threat from commercialization, but the pattern of thought is common. Andrea Fraser, reflecting in 2004 on a work that she produced which consisted of having sex with a collector, puts the same opposition to work for somewhat different ends:

zh: 嗯，是的，那是艺术；我有兴趣提出的问题是，艺术是否就是卖淫——当然，是在隐喻意义上。我碰巧和一个人发生性关系，难道就比我只是卖给他一件作品更像卖淫吗？事实上，对于出售《无题》的DVD，我至今仍远比我制作这件作品时更不舒服。艺术界那种“正常”的销售情境，在我看来，比我与参与收藏者的关系或交换的任何方面都更具剥削性。那才是我失去控制的地方。投机就是从那里开始的。
en: Well, yes, it’s art, and the question I’m interested in posing is  whether art is prostitution – in a metaphorical sense, of course. Is  it any more prostitution because I happen to be having sex with a  man than it would be if I were just selling him a piece? In fact, I  remain much less comfortable with selling the DVDs of ‘Untitled’  than I was with producing the piece. The ‘normal’ sales situation  that one has in the art world feels much more exploitative to me  than any aspect of my relationship with, or the exchange with the  participating collector. That’s where I lose control of it. That’s where  the speculation begins.

zh: 在这一情形中，艺术品的出售对艺术家而言代表一场同时是道德与经济的危机（使艺术家既感到不适又遭到剥削）。这些话语套路或许把对艺术品销售的焦虑，与异化劳动概念以及致力于废除异化劳动的行动主义传统联系起来。但我想考察这里一个更为具体的预设：艺术与商业严重对立。如果说克拉克只是通过联想暗示艺术受到市场的危害，那么在弗雷泽这里，艺术与商业之间的对抗就像这一观念最初被提出时一样明确。在康德表述美的艺术的双重自由时，艺术与销售相对抗的观念已牢固确立。他说，这些特定艺术必须在没有外在目的的意义上是自由的，而且还要“在这样一种意义上是自由的：它们不是一种雇佣职业，因而也不是一种其大小可按确定标准来评判、索取或支付的劳动”。
en: The sale of art, in this scenario, represents a crisis for the artist that is at once moral and economic (subjecting the artist to both discomfort and exploitation). These tropes, perhaps, link anxieties about art sales to the concept of alienated labour and the activist tradition intent on abolishing it. But I want to investigate the more specific assumption, here, that art and commerce are seriously at odds. If Clark only implied by association that art is endangered by the marketplace, in Fraser the antagonism between art and commerce is as explicit as when this idea was first formulated. The conception of art as antagonistic to sales is firmly established by the time of Kant’s formulation of the twofold freedom of the fine arts. These specific arts, he said, must be free in the sense that they have no extrinsic purpose, but also ‘free in the sense of not being a mercenary occupation and hence a kind of labor, whose magnitude can be judged, exacted, or paid for according to a determinate standard’.

zh: 艺术与商业对抗的历史，是艺术得以凌驾于手艺及其他商业活动之上的一个组成部分。
en: The history of art’s antagonism to commerce is a component of art’s elevation above handicraft and other commercial activities.

zh: 当前，艺术机构内部的政治行动主义已从对机构的意识形态批判，转向要求机构向艺术家和艺术工作者（实习生、工作室助手等）支付报酬。
我对艺术与资本主义对抗史的研究，是对艺术中各种“资本主义现实主义”
的反驳；这类立场宣称艺术作品是商品、艺术家是工人，而艺术家与商业相对抗的神话助长了把艺术家当作无酬劳动者加以剥削。我的目的不是支持对设计、工艺与媚俗艺术的谴责以警示艺术家，而是考察艺术内部反资本主义的历史。
en: Currently, political activism within art’s institutions has shifted from the ideological critique of institutions to the demand for artists and art workers (interns, studio assistants and others) to be paid by them.
My inquiry into the history of the antagonism between art and capitalism is a rebuttal to forms of ‘capitalist realism’

in art that declare artworks are commodities, artists are workers, and the myth of the artist as antagonistic to commerce contributes to the exploitation of artists as unpaid labourers. My purpose is not to endorse the condemnation of design, craft and kitsch as a warning to artists but to investigate the history of anti-capitalism within art.

zh: 艺术与商业或销售相对抗这一观念的历史根源何在？在某种意义上可以说，对买卖之腐化的忧虑并不限于艺术领域，而是以这种或那种形式贯穿历史。然而，我心中所想的起源，并不能通过找出这一观念的最初表述而发掘出来。艺术与市场之间的结构性对抗，也不是在文艺复兴时期的个别画家和雕塑家在行会与宫廷这一封建艺术组织内部争取到某些特权时实现的。我们需要解开艺术中对商业的特定拒斥与更为悠久的贵族业余爱好者传统之间的关系；而二者之间相互借用、替换与转化的历史使这项任务变得困难。
en: What is the historical source of the idea that art is antagonistic to commerce or sales? In some sense, we might say, concerns about the corruptions of buying and selling are not limited to the field of art and are present in one form or another throughout history. However, the origin I have in mind is not unearthed by identifying the first formulation of the idea. Nor is the structural antagonism between art and the marketplace realized when individual painters and sculptors in the Renaissance manage to secure certain privileges within the feudal organization of the arts in the guilds and court. We need to unpick the relationship between the specific rejection of commerce in art and the longer tradition of the noble amateur, a task that is hampered by the history of borrowing, substitution and transformation between the two.

zh: 由于业余性对贵族而言是一种规范，并在资产阶级革命后以改变过的形式存留下来，按照拒斥商业的原则对艺术进行改造究竟发生于何时，便难以确切指明，尤其是如果我们把视野局限于观念史。然而，如果我们把注意力集中于艺术不断变化的生产方式，这项考察就能获得一些清晰性。这等于把哲学中的艺术问题，以及艺术话语中艺术与商业的规范性分离，都锚定到对封建主义向资本主义过渡的研究之中——但有一项限定：在这一历史过渡中，艺术并未采用标准的资本主义生产方式，因为后者主要由资本与雇佣劳动之间的对抗构成，而这种对抗在艺术作品的生产中几乎完全缺席。
在封建主义向资本主义过渡的时期，行会制度内部曾占主导的工作社会关系遭到工资制度的对抗，并最终被其吞没。然而，画家和雕塑家并未像手工业者通常那样，从行会成员转变为雇佣劳动者或资本主义雇主。相反，对行会的拒斥走上了一条不同的道路。
en: Since amateurism is a norm for the nobility, and this survives in modified forms after the bourgeois revolutions, the reformation of art according to the principle of the rejection of commerce is difficult to pinpoint, especially if we restrict our view to a history of ideas. Some clarity is brought to this investigation, however, if we focus our attention on the changing mode of production of art. This amounts to indexing the art question in philosophy and the normative separation of art from commerce in art’s discourses to the study of the transition from feudalism to capitalism – with the proviso that this historical passage does not see art adopt a standard capitalist mode of production, since the latter consists principally of a confrontation between capital and wage-labour that is almost entirely absent in the production of artworks.

During the period of transition from feudalism to capitalism the social relations of work which had prevailed within the guild system were opposed and ultimately overrun by the wage system. However, painters and sculptors were not converted from members of the guild to either wage labourers or capitalist employers, as artisans typically were. Instead, the rejection of the guilds took a different turn.

children: 通往艺术市场的漫长道路
The long road to the art market

zh: 一个区别于手工业者的艺术家概念的出现，是那场充满争议的转变的关键要素：绘画和雕塑（及相关艺术）先从机械艺术被重新归入美的艺术，随后又从若干特定艺术转变为一般意义上的艺术。史蒂夫·爱德华兹在论述摄影历史上如何与艺术相区别、以及在摄影内部文献如何与图像相区别时，回顾了这段历程。
en: The emergence of a concept of the artist distinct from the artisan is a vital ingredient of the contested transition from the classification of painting and sculpture (and related arts) from the mechanical arts to the fine arts and, subsequently, from the several specific arts to art in general. Steve Edwards recalls this passage in his account of how photography has historically been distinguished from art and how, within photography, the document has been distinguished from the picture.

zh: 这些对立大多植根于“自由”艺术与“机械”艺术之间的区分……［并］植根于一场旷日持久的斗争，即为提升……画家的地位而进行的斗争，他们力图把自己同车轮匠、制桶匠以及其他常常被归入同一类别的人区分开来。为了做到这一点，他们坚持认为，他们的工作是一门自由艺术，而不是低贱的手工艺（或机械）行业。
en: Most of these oppositions have their roots in the distinction  between the ‘liberal’ and the ‘mechanical arts’ … [and] in a  protracted struggle to raise the status of … painters [who] sought  to distinguish themselves from wheelwrights, barrel-makers, and  others with whom they were frequently classed. To do this they insisted that their work was a liberal art and not a lowly artisanal (or  mechanical) trade.

zh: 艺术问题围绕艺术与手艺之间的关系转动，这种关系不仅把自由艺术置于机械艺术之上，也把业余活动的贵族价值置于商业之上。爱德华兹指出，“艺术家争取地位的长期斗争中，一个决定性的转折点出现在1648年巴黎皇家绘画与雕塑学院建立之时”。
那么，让我们看看这一事件在艺术经济与规范转型的历史中是如何被理解的。
en: The art question pivots around a relationship between art and handicraft that prioritizes not only the liberal arts over the mechanical arts but also the noble value of amateurism over trade. Edwards notes that a ‘decisive turning point in artists’ protracted struggle over status occurred with the establishment of the Académie Royale de Peinture et de Sculpture in Paris in 1648’.
So, let’s look at how this event has been understood in the history of art’s economic and normative transformation.

zh: 辛西娅·怀特与哈里森·怀特在他们那本颇有影响的著作中，论述了艺术的现代制度如何经由皇家学院的建立，从“中世纪画家行会”中产生。他们写道，画家们“在行会限制下愤懑不安”，而皇家学院“起初只是独立于行会，但很快便在权力与声望上支配行会，随后取代了行会”，此后才出现“批评家—画商体系”。
这一高度压缩的叙述在许多方面仍是一份有用的路线图，但叙事的每个部分都需要依据生产关系视角重新审视。例如，行会→学院→艺术市场这一更替叙事，为共时性的戏剧效果牺牲了历时性的细微差别。我们可以部分克服这一点：承认自14世纪起，各种画家与雕塑家学院就与行会并行存在，而皇家学院与行会并行运行了近150年，直到两者都被革命政府废除。
en: Cynthia and Harrison White, in their influential book on the emergence of art’s modern institutions out of the ‘medieval painters’ guilds’ via the founding of the Académie Royale, write that painters ‘chafed under guild restrictions’ and that the Académie Royale ‘was at first merely independent of the guild, but soon dominated and then replaced it in power and prestige’ before the advent of the ‘critic–dealer system’.

This compacted account remains, in many respects, a useful road map, but each section of the narrative needs to be reconsidered according to the perspective of the social relations of production. For instance, the narrative of succession – guild to academy to art market – sacrifices diachronic nuance for synchronic drama. We can overcome this, partly, by acknowledging that various academies for painters and sculptors existed in parallel with the guilds from the fourteenth century onwards and that the Académie Royale ran parallel with the guilds for almost 150 years before they were both abolished by the revolutionary government.

zh: 的确，这些学院从行会与宫廷的双重体系中生长出来，以巩固画家和雕塑家在宫廷中的地位；17世纪建立的皇家学院则将宫廷画家和雕塑家的特权正式化并加以扩展。文艺复兴时期的学院并不是教学机构，但佛罗伦萨设计学院的章程规定，每年选出三名学院成员，前往年轻从业者的工坊拜访，给予友好建议。工坊活动不仅与学院并行进行，而且是学院运作所必需的。然而，讲座从一开始就是学院的常规项目，最初是作为手段，在封建主义设定的条件下把某些艺术——特别是绘画和雕塑——从机械艺术提升为自由艺术；但后来，我认为，它也成为一种方法，用以在社会分工中把艺术家同雇佣劳动者、手工业者、制造商、店主和产业资本家区分开来。
en: Indeed, the academies grew out of the dual system of guild and court to bolster the position of painters and sculptors in the court, and the royal academy established in the seventeenth century formalized and extended the privileges of court painters and sculptors. The Renaissance academy was not a teaching institution, but the statutes of the Florence Academy of Design specify that three members of the academy would be selected annually to visit young practitioners in their workshops to give friendly advice. Workshop activities not only went on in parallel with the academies but were necessary for its functioning. However, from the outset, lectures were a regular feature of the academies, initially as a device to raise the status of certain arts – specifically painting and sculpture – from the mechanical arts to the liberal arts on terms set by feudalism, but also later, I would argue, as a method to differentiate the artist within the social division of labour from the wage-labourer, artisan, manufacturer, shopkeeper and industrial capitalist.

zh: 怀特夫妇把画家在三种历史模式——行会、学院与市场——中的演进，设定为一部从封建束缚中解放出来的线性故事中的一个插曲。这种现代主义叙事遵循一条经济史学家熟悉的路径，即自由主义关于自由放任兴起、对抗看似过时的封建管制与干预形式的叙事。通过美的艺术倡导者如何竭力把行会手工业者指认为机械的复制者，并以此对照院士们受灵感启发、具有原创性、富有学识的活动，来重读这一叙事，颇能说明问题。克里斯蒂安·米歇尔指出，现代主义对学院的批判“与学院当初对行会的批判极为相似”。
我们可以看到，两者都强调对手在机械与手工方面的局限。因此，当怀特夫妇说学院“强调一种新的艺术家概念：他不再是手工业者，也不是兜售货物的低等小贩，而是一个有学问的人，是美与趣味之高尚原则的教师”时，我们也得以瞥见，现代主义把学院拒斥为死记硬背、教条僵化与中央集权的官僚机构之地，其中包含着怎样的利害关系。
en: White and White’s procession of painters in three historical modes – guild, academy and market – is set up as an episode in a linear tale of emancipation from feudal constraints. This modernist narrative follows a path familiar to historians of economics, namely the liberal tale of the rise of laissez-faire against seemingly obsolete forms of feudal regulation and intervention. It is instructive to reread this narrative through the extraordinary efforts of the advocates of the fine arts to designate guild artisans as mechanical copyists in contrast with the inspired, original and scholarly activities of the academicians. Christian Michel points out that the modernist critique of the academy ‘strongly resembled the critiques levelled by the Académie against the guild’.

Both, we can observe, stressed the mechanical and manual limitations of its opponent. So, when White and White say the academy ‘emphasized a new conception of the artist: no longer an artisan or a low-caste hawker of wares, he was instead a learned man, a teacher of the high principles of beauty and taste’, we get a glimpse, also, at what was at stake in the modernist rejection of the academy as a place of rote learning, doctrinal stiffness and centralized bureaucracy.

zh: 怀特夫妇等人主张，艺术作为从赞助制向艺术市场过渡的结果，从诸艺术中浮现出来。这一论证的优点是指向结构性经济变化，缺点是聚焦流通变化而非艺术的生产方式：它阻碍了对以下变化进行分析：艺术家工作室及其供应链的社会关系，艺术家与其助手之间的分工，艺术家、画商与艺术导师之间的分工，等等。尽管中世纪和文艺复兴时期的画家与雕塑家在手工业工坊中集体工作这一事实并非无人注意，艺术史家还是倾向于把注意力集中在某些典范性的个人身上，常常夸大这些人在多大程度上独立于手工业工坊体系运作，以及在多大程度上拒绝使用助手和学徒。
en: White and White and others argue that art emerges from the arts as a result of the transition from patronage to the art market. This argument has the advantage of pointing towards structural economic changes but the disadvantage of focusing on changes in circulation rather than art’s mode of production: it blocks the analysis of changes in the social relations of the artist’s studio and its supply chains, the division of labour between artists and their assistants, the division of labour between the artist, the art dealer and the art tutor, and so forth. While it has certainly not gone unnoticed that painters and sculptors in the Middle Ages and the Renaissance worked collectively in artisan workshops, art historians have tended to focus their attention on certain exemplary individuals and often exaggerated the degree to which they operated outside the artisan workshop system, and abjured the use of assistants and apprentices.

zh: 艺术与手艺之间的边界，是作为行会与学院之间的区分而锻造出来的，二者都是男性专有的领域；但到18世纪末，这条分界线获得了一种明确带性别色彩的性质。乔舒亚·雷诺兹爵士曾由他的姐姐——一位有造诣的水彩画家——教习绘画，他带头禁止水彩画参加年度夏季展览；用头发制成的画、剪纸以及其他兼有浓重手工艺和女性气质气息的图像，也一并被排除。相比之下，承认行会师傅对学徒、日工及更广义的家庭的依赖，比认清在工作室里为某位艺术家的艺术生产作出贡献的全体工人，要容易得多。这种误认内建于学院体系之中。
en: The border between art and handicraft is forged as a differentiation between the guild and the academy, both exclusively male provinces, but by the end of the eighteenth century the dividing line takes on an emphatically gendered quality. Sir Joshua Reynolds, who had been taught to paint by his sister, an accomplished watercolourist, led the charge to disallow watercolour paintings from the annual summer exhibition, alongside pictures made of hair, paper cut-outs and other images with a strong whiff both of craft and of femininity. By comparison, it is easier to acknowledge the guild master’s dependence on apprentices, day-labourers and their household more generally than it is to recognize the full cast of workers who contribute to the production of art by an individual artist in a studio. This misrecognition was built into the academy system.

zh: 学院并非自给自足的机构。例如，皇家学院在很大程度上似乎是从行会中吸纳最优秀的画家和雕塑家。学院并不教授任何技术意义上的绘画或雕塑，而是仅接纳能够通过提交一件“入选作品”证明其在某一门美的艺术中具备娴熟能力的候选人。“在执笔和培养良好眼力方面当过学徒——先临摹素描和版画，再对立体形态写生——是进入皇家学院的条件，但学院本身并不教授素描。”
因此，皇家学院仍依赖某种正式或非正式的学徒训练，作为其学生教育的预备阶段。
en: The academy was not a self-sufficient body. For instance, the Académie Royale appeared for the most part to draw the best of the painters and sculptors from the guild. Academies did not teach painting or sculpture in any technical sense but restricted admission to candidates who could demonstrate facility in one of the fine arts through the presentation of a ‘reception piece’. ‘An apprenticeship in handling a pencil and acquiring a good eye, first by copying drawings and engravings and then by drawing from three-dimensional forms, was a condition of admission to the Académie, but drawing was not taught there.’
As such, the Académie continued to rely on a type of formal or informal apprenticeship as a preliminary stage of education for its students.

zh: 关于从手工业者到艺术家的转变的叙述，从两个个体生产者的狭隘视角来看待艺术生产社会关系的历史转型。实际上，这一转变由先前在工坊内进行的大量任务在地理上的分散构成。合作工坊中的每一个手工业者都能胜任若干后来成为专门职业的工作：熟练工人、工具制造者、材料供应者、设计者、教师和商人。因此，手工业者并非只转变为艺术家，也转变为所有其他这些专门职业。于是，从手工业者到艺术家的转变，伴随着从手工业者到材料供应商、从手工业者到技术员或助手、从手工业者到教师或画商等等的转变。也就是说，工坊内部的分工被转化为以市场交换为中介的整个社会中的社会分工。
en: Accounts of the passage from the artisan to the artist view the historical transformation of the social relations of artistic production from the narrow perspective of two individual producers. Actually, this transition consists of the geographical dispersal of numerous tasks previously conducted within the workshop. Each single artisan within the cooperative workshop was capable of several jobs that would later become specialisms, namely skilled worker, manufacturer of tools, supplier of materials, designer, teacher and dealer. Hence, the artisan does not exclusively turn into the artist but also into all these other specialisms. The passage from the artisan to the artist is accompanied therefore by the passage from the artisan to the materials supplier, from the artisan to the technician or assistant, from the artisan to the teacher or dealer, and so on. That is to say, the division of labour within the workshop is converted into a social division of labour in society as a whole mediated by market exchange.

zh: 让我们暂时聚焦于封建主义向资本主义过渡期间艺术劳动重组在空间上的方面：我们必须考虑的不仅是艺术劳动发生的空间，即从手工业工坊到艺术家工作室的转变，更根本地，是从行会工坊内部一系列活动的整合，向这些活动在空间上分散的转变——它们后来发生在工作室、画廊、艺术学校、博物馆、代工工坊之内及彼此之间，也发生在为艺术的生产与流通提供工具、机械和材料的所有供应链之中。从商业性的手工业者那里购买供应品，以及伴随这场从工坊出走而发展起来的其他一切专门职业，把技术分工转化为社会分工。商业供应商削弱了学徒为“师傅”完成这项工作的需要，因而巩固了绘画和雕塑的学院教育体系；该体系由艺术家与艺术教师之间的社会分工构成，从而把工作室与艺术学校分离开来。
en: Focusing for a moment on the spatial aspect of the reorganization of artistic labour during the transition from feudalism to capitalism, we must consider not only the spaces in which artistic labour takes place, as a passage from the artisanal workshop to the artist’s studio, but more fundamentally as the transition from the integration of a range of activities within the guild workshop to the spatial dispersal of activities that come to take place within and between the studio, gallery, art school, museum, fabricators’ workshop and all the supply chains that provide their tools, machinery and materials for the production and circulation of art. The purchasing of supplies from commercial artisans, and all the other specialisms that developed out of this exodus from the workshop, converted the technical division of labour into a social division of labour. Commercial suppliers diminished the need for apprentices to complete this work for the ‘master’ and therefore consolidated the academic system of education for painting and sculpture, which consists of a social division of labour between the artist and the art teacher, thereby separating the studio from the art school.

zh: 在资本主义门槛处，艺术劳动的社会分工凭借艺术作品生产者与其收藏者之间专门中介者的创新，重新界定了有别于手工业者的艺术家。今天，我们把画商或画廊主设想为一种代理人，把艺术家引入艺术市场的方向；但从历史上看，艺术作品专业销售者的引入，把销售任务从生产者自己手中拿走，因而在艺术家与直接面对付费顾客之间充当了一种缓冲。宫廷赞助的惯例长期以来掩盖了赞助人与画家之间的经济交易，但在工坊里卖画的行会画家别无选择，只能把产品卖给市场。学院体系的创立者抓住了这些区分。
en: The social division of artistic labour at the threshold of capitalism redefined the artist as distinct from the artisan by the innovation of specialist mediators between the producers of artworks and their collectors. Today, we think of the art dealer or gallerist as an agent who funnels the artist in the direction of the art market, but historically the introduction of the specialist seller of works of art took the task of sales away from the producers themselves and acted, therefore, as a kind of buffer between the artist and the direct encounter with paying customers. Conventions of courtly patronage had long suppressed the economic transaction between patrons and painters, but guild painters selling paintings from their workshop had no choice but to sell their products to the market. These distinctions were seized on by the founders of the academy system.

zh: 学院把自己与行会区分开来，确保其成员区别于手工业者，并主张其学生区别于学徒；这重新塑造了画家和雕塑家，使他们成为学识的产物而非手艺的产物。整个计划的症候，是1648年（并在1777年再次出现）的一个插曲：皇家学院颁布章程，宣布那些“希望开店经营他人之手的绘画、素描和雕塑，出售颜料、金箔及其他绘画和雕塑艺术辅料者……必须申请加入画家—雕塑家共同体［行会］”。
这一章程不是艺术与商业相对抗这一观念的终极来源，但它对于该观念在维护它的新社会制度内部得到巩固至关重要。正是这一章程，以及与之相应的争论和实践——无论在法国学院内部，还是在国外任何重述其模式的地方——把作为个人品格问题而贬低商业的高贵姿态，转化为一种将艺术与手艺、工业和企业区别开来的定义的基础。
en: The academy distinguished itself from the guild, secured the distinction of its members from artisans and asserted the distinction of its students from apprentices, which recast the painter and sculptor as the product of scholarship rather than handicraft. Symptomatic of the entire project is an episode in 1648 (and again in 1777) when the Académie Royale issued a statute proclaiming those who ‘wish to open a shop and trade in pictures, drawings, and sculptures by other hands, sell colors, gilding, and other accessories of the arts of painting and sculpture … shall be required to seek admission to the Community [Guild] of Painter-Sculptors’.

This statute is not the ultimate source of the idea that art is antagonistic to commerce but it was essential to the consolidation of that idea within new social institutions that upheld it. It is this statute, and the debates and practices that corresponded to it, both within the French academy and wherever its model was reiterated abroad, that converted the nobility of disparaging commerce as a matter of individual character into the basis of a definition of art as distinct from handicraft, industry and business.

zh: 由于具有正式资格的行会成员拥有开店的专属权利，禁止院士开店的章程可以被解读为行会的胜利，以及学院承认自己无法将这种权利授予其成员。事实上，从工坊到学院的历史转变把美的艺术家重塑为有学问的个人，却使艺术家不能再从事手工业者仍在进行的那一整套广泛活动。在某种意义上，它构成了对画家和雕塑家自由与能动性的明显削减。然而，17世纪学院的商业禁令是沙龙展创办的前提——沙龙展为学院成员提供机会，使他们无须开店即可向公众展出，并向赞助人和收藏家宣传自己——也是画商兴起的前提，而画商把美的艺术中有学问的实践者与直接经济交易隔绝开来。因此，即便章程本身无权禁止艺术家开店，他们总体上也没有这样做，而是遵循学院先例，为公众举办展览，并通过画商和画廊主销售作品。换言之，学院商业禁令的后果以客观的社会方式把艺术的生产方式界定为与市场对抗，从而为把这一命令作为抽象规范延续下去提供了物质基础。
en: Since the freemen of the guilds held the exclusive right to own a shop, the statute forbidding academicians from opening a shop can be read as a victory of the guilds and the admission that the academy could not award such a right to its members. In fact, the historical transition from the workshop to the academy, which recast the fine artist as a scholarly individual, blocked the breadth of activities that continued to be practised by artisans. In some sense, then, it constituted a palpable reduction of freedom and agency for the painter and sculptor. Nevertheless, the ban on commerce in the seventeenth-century academy was the precondition for the inauguration of the salons – opportunities for its members to exhibit to the public and advertise themselves to patrons and collectors without opening a shop – and the rise of art dealers, which sealed off the scholarly practitioner of the fine arts from direct economic transactions. So, even when the statute itself had no power to prohibit artists from opening shops, they did not on the whole do so, but followed academic precedent in staging exhibitions for the public and selling works via dealers and gallerists. In other words, the consequences of the academic ban on commerce defined art’s mode of production as antagonistic to the market in objective social terms that provided material grounds for the command to be perpetuated as an abstract norm.

zh: 关于艺术家范畴如何从更悠久的手工业生产史中产生的标准叙事，强调一场把精英少数提升到平庸的零工手工业者大众之上的运动。无论论证的是文艺复兴的伟大画家、雕塑家和建筑师事实上就是艺术家，还是把“艺术家”一词留给18世纪之后以现代意义使用该词的后来世代，故事都一样：艺术家在历史上经由一个与手工业者相区分的过程而出现。然而，艺术家与手工业者之间的区分从来都不是绝对的，也从未以确定无疑的方式被主张。这与行会制度漫长时期中手工业者同所有其他工人的区分形成鲜明对照。行会依靠绝对区分来运作，并对这些区分加以规制和执行。例如，服完学徒期的人与未服完学徒期的人之间的差别是显而易见的。可以出示证据和证词来确定事实，解决关于某个特定个人地位的争议。
en: The standard narrative of the emergence of the category of the artist out of a longer history of handicraft production stresses the campaign to elevate an elite minority above the mediocre mass of jobbing artisans. Whether it is argued that the great painters, sculptors and architects of the Renaissance were in fact artists, or whether the word itself is saved for later generations after the eighteenth century that used the word ‘artist’ in the modern sense, the story is the same: the artist emerges historically through a process of distinction from the artisan. Yet the differentiation of the artist from the artisan has never been absolute or asserted with certainty. This contrasts sharply with the differentiation of the artisan from all other workers during the long period of the guild system. Guilds operated with absolute distinctions that they regulated and enforced. For instance, the difference between an individual who had served an apprenticeship and another who had not was palpable. Evidence and testimony could be presented to determine the facts and resolve disputes about the status of a particular individual.

zh: 相反，艺术家的地位以及美的艺术凌驾于手艺之上的提升，始终是相对的而非绝对的。这种质量与地位上的新型相对区分，是通过一场针对手工业画家和雕塑家的话语运动实现的：把他们仅仅与机械技术和低微的准备性工作联系起来——能复制而不能发明，有技能而无才华，如此等等。一个例子可以显示这些细微而模糊的差别是如何被表述出来的。在皇家学院早年，围绕学院绘画中应重视色彩还是素描的问题，出现了一场原则性辩论。“色彩与研磨颜料和给布上色这一手工任务相联系”，因此关于色彩与线条的辩论，是一种关于美的艺术与手艺之间关系的编码化话语。色彩作为一种物质，是手工业者的领域，因此在色彩方面，院士似乎有两种方法可以用来标示自己与手艺的分离。要么把色彩贬低到素描和线条之下的低等地位，要么赋予色彩一种它在行会那里并不具有的新的智性意义。色彩要么被排除，要么被形而上学地提升，以此遭到否定。
en: The status of the artist, on the contrary, and the elevation of the fine arts above handicraft, was always relative rather than absolute. This new relative differentiation of quality and status was achieved through a discursive campaign against artisan painters and sculptors by associating them with nothing more than mechanical techniques and menial preparatory tasks, capable of copying but not inventing, skilled but not talented, and so forth. An example may show how these nuanced vague differences were articulated. In the early years of the Académie Royale a principled debate arose over the question of whether to privilege colour or drawing in academic painting. ‘Colour was associated with the manual task of grinding pigments and staining cloths’, therefore debates on colour and line were a coded discourse on the relationship between the fine arts and handicraft. Colour, as a substance, was the province of the artisan, and therefore the academician appeared to have two methods available for marking a separation from handicraft with regard to colour. Either colour could be relegated to a low status below drawing and line, or colour could be assigned a new intellectual significance that it did not have for the guilds. Colour was negated by elimination or metaphysical elevation.

zh: 可以预料，色彩与素描之争从未以任何一方获胜而告终，但模式已经确立：美的艺术（以及随后的一般艺术）将凌驾于手艺之上，艺术家将凌驾于手工业者之上，其依据不是显而易见的证据或绝对区分，而是对不可测量品质的判断、由未经确保的等级制引导的比较、对未被测绘之边界的充满不确定性的边境管控、对无形属性的不可计算的度量，以及对相对区分的不受法律约束的巡查。这也反映在以下替代之中：行会享有的众多具体自由（在城界内经商、开店、招收学徒等自由）被替换为美的艺术（以及后来的一般艺术）那种未加规定的抽象自由。
en: Predictably, the quarrel of colour versus drawing was never settled one way or the other, but the pattern was set: the fine arts (and subsequently art in general) would be elevated above handicraft, and the artist above the artisan, not on the basis of palpable evidence or absolute distinctions but through judgements of immeasurable qualities, comparisons guided by unsecured hierarchies, uncertain border controls of unmapped boundaries, the incalculable measurements of incorporeal properties and the lawless policing of relative differentiations. This is also reflected in the replacement of the numerous specific freedoms enjoyed by the guild (the freedom to trade within the city limits, the freedom to open a shop, the freedom to take on apprentices, and so on) with the unspecified abstract freedom of the fine arts (and later art in general).

zh: 艺术与工艺和工业之差别在确定性上的相对缺乏，明显体现在它凌驾于二者之上这一备受争议的提升之中。正因如此，艺术才是一个会引发去魅式、揭穿式批判的范畴；也正因如此，有时“艺术”一词看起来仿佛是一个空洞的能指，是精英主义与特权资格的委婉语。然而与此同时，这种不确定性也正是艺术为何被珍视为不可还原为工具理性、艺术活动为何被视为异化劳动的死敌、艺术作品为何被视为超出商品形式的核心原因。在我的分析中，艺术范畴的不确定性，是艺术借以把自己提升到手艺之上的那些社会过程的必然结果，这些过程包括：对手工业者的歪曲呈现、对艺术家的自由与原创性的夸大、对有偿和无酬工人为艺术生产所作贡献的压制，以及关键的——艺术家与市场之间中介机构的增殖。
en: The relative lack of determinacy of art’s difference from craft and industry is evident in its contested elevation above them. This is why art is a category that triggers the demystifying and debunking critique of it, and why, at times, it has appeared as if the word ‘art’ is an empty signifier and a euphemism for elitism and entitlement. At the same time, however, this indeterminacy is at the heart of why art is cherished as irreducible to instrumental reason, why artistic activity is taken to be anathema to alienated labour, and why the artwork is seen to exceed the commodity-form. In my analysis, the indeterminacy of the category of art is a necessary consequence of the social processes by which art elevated itself above handicraft, including the misrepresentation of the artisan, exaggerations of the freedom and originality of the artist, suppressions of the contribution of paid and unpaid workers to the production of art, and, crucially, the proliferation of intermediary agencies between the artist and the market.

zh: 艺术中的商业禁忌虽然并未把美的艺术与手艺之间的相对区分完全转化为绝对差异，却是艺术家与手工业者之区分得到生活化实行的一种方式，并在艺术制度、经济与教育学中具体化时成为该区分的客观相关物。艺术家与其助手、代工者、技术人员和实习生之间的关系——最近已在艺术劳动政治中被提出——见证了那种作为学院体系奠基姿态的对手艺的退避仍在延续。它存留于两种现象中：对艺术中手艺在场的长久焦虑，以及悬在艺术家与由直接和间接助手组成的配角阵容之间关系上的持续问号。
en: Though not quite converting the relative distinction of the fine arts from handicraft into an absolute difference, the taboo on commerce in art was one of the ways in which the distinction between the artist and artisan was lived out, and became an objective correlate of that distinction when it was concretized in art’s institutions, economies and pedagogy. The relationship between artists and their assistants, fabricators, technicians and interns – which has been raised recently within a politics of artistic labour – testifies to the continuation of the withdrawal from handicraft that was the founding gesture of the academy system. It survives in both the perennial anxiety about the presence of handicraft in art and the persistent question mark over the relationship between the artist and a supporting cast of direct and indirect assistants.

zh: 在观念史中，“艺术问题”产生于未能确定各门美的艺术所共享的原则或共同特征。在社会史中，这个问题则以学院长期开展的运动为标志：贬抑手艺，并把有学问的画家和雕塑家提升到手工业者之上。把绘画和雕塑从机械艺术中提升出来的运动，并未成功将它们牢固地安置在自由艺术之内。面对这一失败，人们铸造了一个新范畴——美的艺术，它在封建艺术体制内把少数特定艺术归入机械艺术与自由艺术之间某个未加指明的位置。当封建生产方式被资本主义生产方式取代时，艺术对手艺的优越地位借由把艺术那种高贵的反商业性（反资本主义的前资本主义版本）重构为对市场需求无动于衷的原创作品生产而存续下来；从19世纪起，这常常被表述为与资产阶级、公众、时尚和富人趣味的对立。
en: In the history of ideas, ‘the art question’ arises out of the failure to determine the shared principles or common features of the various fine arts. In social history, this question is marked by the long campaign by the academy to undermine handicraft and elevate scholarly painters and sculptors above artisans. The campaign to lift painting and sculpture out of the mechanical arts did not succeed in lodging them firmly within the liberal arts. In the face of this failure a new category was coined, the fine arts, which classified a small number of specific arts in some unspecified place between the mechanical and liberal arts within the feudal regime of the arts. When the feudal mode of production was superseded by the capitalist mode of production, the elevation of art above handicraft survived by reconstituting art’s noble antagonism to commerce (a pre-capitalist version of anti-capitalism) as the production of original works indifferent to market demand, often expressed from the nineteenth century onwards as an opposition to the bourgeoisie, the public, fashion and the taste of the wealthy.

zh: 因此，聚焦于艺术对商业的敌意，可以构成对行会向自由放任过渡之标准叙事的挑战，或者，在艺术史中，对赞助制向艺术市场过渡之标准叙事的挑战。在关于艺术从封建主义向资本主义过渡的叙述中，商品化过程被夸大了。在考虑艺术的特殊性时，不应聚焦于艺术对象的性质或经典化过程，而必须更多地关注艺术生产的社会关系。艺术中对商业的敌意——它常常显得像是意识形态的、浪漫主义的或一种禁忌——才是艺术那有别于雇佣劳动、手艺、商业和工业的标志性劳动范畴得以形成的真正历史前提。
en: Focus on the hostility of art to commerce may thus act as a challenge to the standard narrative of the transition from the guild to laissez-faire or, in art history, from patronage to the art market. There is an overstatement of processes of commodification in accounts of art’s passage from feudalism to capitalism. When considering the specificity of art, rather than focusing on the nature of art objects or processes of canonization, more attention must be paid to the social relations of artistic production. The hostility to commerce in art, which often appears to be ideological or romantic or a taboo, is the real historical precondition for the formation of art’s characteristic category of labour distinct from wage-labour, handicraft, trade and industry.

zh: 我将区分“艺术”（art）、“诸艺术”（arts）和“美的艺术”（fine arts）这三个术语。尽管它们常被当作可互换的术语，日常语言也允许把它们用作同义词，但我将用它们指称劳动分类的历史形式。“诸艺术”以复数形式出现，指烹饪、捕鱼、编篮和修辞等具体技能实践；这些实践在历史上被分为机械艺术与自由艺术。“美的艺术”是附属于绘画和雕塑的一组特定艺术。单数形式的“艺术”指一般意义上的艺术概念，它不可还原为绘画、雕塑或任何特定艺术。艺术的一般性概念最早由耶拿浪漫派以“什么是文学？”这一问题加以表述。这个问题标志着从众多特定艺术向一般艺术的过渡。对他们而言，文学不被狭义地设想为若干艺术之一，而被设想为一种抽象：“被当作文学来考察的艺术……［以及］被当作艺术之本质来考察的文学”。见 Philippe Lacoue-Labarthe and Jean-Luc Nancy,

children: The Literary Absolute: The Theory of Literature in German Romanticism

zh: , New York: State University of New York Press, 1988, p. 83。
en: I will distinguish the terms ‘art’, ‘arts’ and ‘fine arts’. Although these terms are often treated as interchangeable, and common language allows them to be used as synonyms, I will use them to refer to historical forms of the classification of labour. ‘Arts’, in the plural, refers to specific skilled practices such as cooking, fishing, basket weaving and rhetoric, which historically were divided in to the mechanical and liberal arts. ‘The fine arts’ are the group of specific arts attached to painting and sculpture. ‘Art’ in the singular refers to the concept of art in general, which is not reducible to painting, sculpture or any of the specific arts. The concept of art in its generality is first formulated by the Jena Romantics as the question: ‘what is literature?’ This question is marked by transition from the numerous specific arts to art in general. For them literature is conceived not narrowly as one of several arts but as an abstraction: ‘art considered as literature … [and] literature considered as the essence of art’. See Philippe Lacoue-Labarthe and Jean-Luc Nancy,

children: The Literary Absolute: The Theory of Literature in German Romanticism

en: , New York: State University of New York Press, 1988, p. 83.

zh: 诗与音乐一直包含在自由艺术之内，因此，对把绘画、雕塑和建筑归类为机械艺术的挑战，是从不包含它们的“设计艺术”观念开始的。后来诗、音乐、绘画、雕塑和舞蹈被归为美的艺术，但确切的选择从未完全固定。
en: Poetry and music had always been included within the liberal arts, and therefore the challenge to the classification of painting, sculpture and architecture as mechanical arts began without them in the idea of the arts of design. Later poetry, music, painting, sculpture and dance were grouped as the fine arts, but the exact selection was never completely settled.

At one end of the scale is the copying of nature (‘the representation of a natural form which consists simply of drawing lines and mixing colours is considered to be work of a mechanical kind’), and at the other end is the genius painter (‘an ingenious and learned Author; as he invents and produces thoughts quite his own’). How are works of art of various kinds related to the mental states of artists or viewers, to physical objects, or to abstract visual, auditory or linguistic structures? en: Marx explains: ‘the numerous analogies and links connecting them, division of labour in the interior of a society, and that in the interior of a workshop, differ not only in degree, but also in kind. The analogy appears most indisputable where there is an invisible bond uniting the various branches of trade. For instance the cattle-breeder produces hides, the tanner makes the hides into leather, and the shoemaker, the leather into boots. Here the thing produced by each of them is but a step towards the final form, which is the product of all their labours combined. There are, besides, all the various industries that supply the cattle-breeder, the tanner, and the shoemaker with the means of production. Now it is quite possible to imagine, with Adam Smith, that the difference between the above social division of labour, and the division in manufacture, is merely subjective, exists merely for the observer, who, in a manufacture, can see with one glance, all the numerous operations being performed on one spot, while in the instance given above, the spreading out of the work over great areas, and the great number of people employed in each branch of labour, obscure the connexion. But what is it that forms the bond between the independent labours of the cattle-breeder, the tanner, and the shoemaker? It is the fact that their respective products are commodities. What, on the other hand, characterises division of labour in manufactures? The fact that the detail labourer produces no commodities. It is only the common product of all the detail labourers that becomes a commodity. Division of labour in society is brought about by the purchase and sale of the products of different branches of industry, while the connexion between the detail operations in a workshop, is due to the sale of the labour-power of several workmen to one capitalist, who applies it as combined labour-power.’ Karl Marx,
